sentences.text:
M/S. Besco Limited & Ors vs Unknown on 22 March, 2023
Author: Bibek Chaudhuri

Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
22.03.2023
Srimanta Crr/1044/2023

In the matter of : M/s. Besco Limited & Ors.
Mr. Ayan Bhattacharjee, Mr. Santanu Talukdar, Mr. Rajib Mullick, Ms. S. Mukherjee ...for the
petitioners.
During the period between 2016 to 2018 the opposite party no. 2 raised invoices in the name of the petitioner claiming payment of the dues as per the invoices.
The petitioners failed to make such payment.

Subsequently on 27th August, 2019 upon an application filed by the opposite party no. 2,
the Chairman, West Bengal State Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council and Director,
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, West Bengal issued a memo advising the petitioner/company to appear in a conciliation, conciliatory process, however, failed.

entities.text: West Bengal State Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, West Bengal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Thereafter on 13 th February, 2020 notice demanding payment of unpaid operational debt due under Section 8 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016 read with Rule 5 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Rule,
2016 was issued to the petitioner no. 1/company requiring them to pay the said amount.
According to the opposite party no. 2, the said amount was not paid.

Subsequently on 22 nd November, 2022 on the basis of a written complaint submitted by the opposite party no. 2 a criminal case was initiated against the petitioner no. 1/company and its Directors/authorized representatives being Nagerbazer Police Station Case No. 444 dated 22nd November, 2022 under Sections 420/406 of the Indian Penal Code.

At the outset, this Court is of the view that the first two grounds cannot be entertained by this Court because of the fact that the opposite party no. 2 went on taking measures available before other authorities for realization of the debt.
Secondly no resolution process under IBC has been adopted against the petitioner no. 1.
However, it is to be looked into as to whether the debt has already been liquidated or not.

If the debt M/S. Besco Limited & Ors vs Unknown on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102791344/
1 is liquidated no criminal liability is said to be ensued against the petitioners.

entities.text: debt M/S. Besco Limited & Ors vs Unknown
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the reason the instant revision is admitted.

Petitioners are directed to serve notice upon the private opposite party under registered speed post with acknowledgement due and file affidavit-of-service within three weeks from the date of this order.
The State of West Bengal be served through the learned Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta.
In the meantime, the investigation shall continue but the Investigating Officer is restrained from taking any coercive step against the petitioner nos. 2 to 4 for a period of six weeks.
Liberty to mention.

( Bibek Chaudhuri, J. )
